title: DR01 ·
headline: A paid ad with one job: show a stranger that 100% of the gift reaches patient care, and that Watsi shows the receipts.
story: Mackinnon, Watsi's Executive Director, says it three ways: not 90%, every dollar; 100% of your donation on Watsi goes to patient care; and every payment, just the actual numbers, over the real transparency sheet. Button: trust is earned, not assumed.

This is the gate ad for the batch: Sonam asked to land this one first and then copy its banner treatment to the rest. Dignified and joyful, never guilt. Loop: “How much reaches the patient?” opens at 0:00 and closes on “100%”.
do: Hook text on frame 1, no logo, no name.
Write the word Watsi in the caption after “donation on”. No logo graphic.
Big number moment on “100%”, then gone.
Show one real receipt row from the transparency sheet.
Keep the approved top banner as it is, letters spaced.
dont: No logo anywhere before the end card. Her tee already shows it.
No surgery, wound or patient pictures. No guilt.
No reused clinic-entrance, waiting-room or patient-hug shots.

transcript:
Auto-transcript of the three Mackinnon takes this ad uses (Watsi Medellín, Interviews & Mackinnon Scripts, 28 Jul 2026). Times are mm:ss.s in each file. The auto-transcript wrote WOTC / WotC for Watsi; it is corrected below.
--- Mincho5163.MP4 ---
[00:02.6] Someone asked me why I joined Watsi.
[00:05.1] I'd spent years in huge organizations, the UN, big NGOs, organizations that do important work, genuinely, but I'd also watched a lot of funding disappear into systems, overhead, bureaucracy, the gap between the dollar that was given and the person who needed it.
[00:20.5] It could have done so much good.
[00:23.1] Then I met Watsi, and the model is simple in the best possible way.
[00:26.9] A patient needs care, we share their story, donors give, the money goes to the hospital, patient receives treatment, and donors always know their impact.
[00:35.3] That's it, 100% of donations go to care, not 90%, not most of it, every dollar, and you hear what happens.
[00:43.6] Even when the outcome isn't what we hoped for, surgery doesn't always go as planned, and we share those stories too.
[00:49.8] And I also think that's what helps build trust, not pretending that every story has a perfect ending, but being honest about what happens.
[00:57.0] I trust this model because I've seen it work thousands of times in dozens of countries for patients and donors who have never met and will never meet and are nonetheless connected in a real way.
[01:08.4] That connection is what we do, and it's a dream to be building it with our team and our community around the world.
[01:18.9] How do you feel? [do not use: crew talk]
[01:19.7] Good. [do not use: crew talk]
--- Mincho5149.MP4 ---
[00:00.6] And let's go. [do not use: crew talk]
[00:02.3] So, how much does Watsi keep?
[00:05.7] 100% of your donation on Watsi goes to patient care.
[00:09.2] I say that simply because it's true.
[00:11.6] That's been true since we launched in 2012, and it's still true today.
[00:15.6] Our operating costs, our staff, technology, infrastructure are covered by a separate pool of philanthropic support that I fundraise for.
[00:23.6] That funding is what makes our 100% model possible, and thank you to those who give to it.
[00:29.6] You can always see our full financials in real time, receipts for the hospital, not just annual but monthly financial statements, and details about each of our medical partners in a public doc on our website that's updated in real time.
[00:42.7] Every payment we've made to every medical partner, no summaries, no abstractions, just the actual numbers.
[00:49.6] And this is what radical transparency can really look like.
[00:54.4] Okay, that should be okay. [do not use: crew talk]
--- Mincho5172.MP4 ---
[00:04.9] Radical transparency isn't just a phrase we put in a values document or paste on our website for everyone to see.
[00:24.3] It means our financial records are publicly available.
[00:27.8] It means you can see every dollar we've ever paid to every medical partner.
[00:33.6] It means if something goes wrong, we tell you.
[00:36.6] And we choose that path, and we've done it since Watsi launched in 2012.
[00:41.8] We do it because we believe that trust is earned, not assumed.
[00:45.8] In a world where it's getting harder to know who or what to believe, our only answer is to show more, not less.
